**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Sparkling:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — the most likely hiding place — contains only standard licence-scope limits (backup-only copying, internal-use documentation copies, no assignment/sublicence, no reverse engineering, use only as authorised, protective precautions). None of these limit what businesses we may run or what products we may buy or build.
- **§ 19 (Non-Solicitation of Employees)** is a mutual one-year no-hire covenant binding both parties, not a competitive restraint, and is handled under the non-solicitation rule rather than this one.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** is time-of-essence and notices boilerplate.
- Text searches for "compet", "develop / market / engage in / similar software", "exclusiv" and "shall not" surfaced only a non-exclusive licence grant (§ 2, § 16(b)), the confidentiality carve-out for independently developed information (§ 14(c) — which affirmatively preserves our development freedom), and standard boilerplate.

This satisfies the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer), so the fallback narrowing is unnecessary and no edit was made.
